title: National Restaurant Association homepage: general industry landing page
answer: This source is the National Restaurant Association's landing page, a general membership and industry resource page. Its most useful point for hospitality readers is that the association supports restaurants of every size at every level of government and describes the industry as the nation's second-largest private sector employer. It lists programs on nutrition, utility disruptions, careers, events, and news. It does not mention AI, drive-thru automation, kitchen robotics, or predictive ordering, so it cannot support those specific claims.

sections.body: The National Restaurant Association publishes this page. It is the association's public landing page, not a research report or an article. The text presents the association's mission, member resources, advocacy role, programs, events, and news. It states no publication date.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page says the National Restaurant Association works to help members build customer loyalty, find financial success, and provide rewarding careers in foodservice. It offers a free guide to help restaurant teams reduce risk, prepare for public safety incidents, and respond with confidence. It says the association supports restaurants of every size at every level of government and describes the restaurant industry as the nation's second-largest private sector employer. It promotes Kids LiveWell, a free marketing program that helps restaurants offer better-for-you meal options to parents dining with children, with menu items meeting the latest nutrition criteria. It describes Always Ready: Utility Disruptions, a guide that prepares operators for power, gas, or water outages and outlines preparations, recovery, and actions during an outage. It lists webinars, podcasts, industry events, and conferences. One upcoming webinar covers high-performing beverage categories, including specialty soft drinks, energy beverages, premium refreshers, alcohol-to-go, and emerging beverage trends. Another webinar explores how the restaurant industry equips people with leadership, problem-solving, and customer service skills. It mentions the Richard E. Marriott Golf Invitational as the largest event for the Restaurant Advocacy Fund. It offers news and information to help operators run a successful restaurant. It also mentions the Made in Restaurants: Industry Careers in America report, which draws on national surveys of current restaurant employees, former restaurant employees, and adults who have never worked in the industry. The page does not discuss AI, automation, robotics, or predictive ordering.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source states that the restaurant industry is the nation's second-largest private sector employer. It names Kids LiveWell, Always Ready: Utility Disruptions, the Richard E. Marriott Golf Invitational, and the Made in Restaurants: Industry Careers in America report. It says the golf invitational is the largest event for the Restaurant Advocacy Fund. It says the Made in Restaurants report draws on national surveys of current restaurant employees, former restaurant employees, and adults who have never worked in the industry. It gives no figures or claims about AI, drive-thru automation, kitchen robotics, or predictive ordering.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in hospitality would find this source useful only as background on the National Restaurant Association's general priorities and member resources. It shows the association's focus on advocacy, risk and safety guides, nutrition programs, workforce careers, events, and news. It does not provide evidence for AI drive-thru, kitchen robotics, or predictive ordering, so it cannot support the industry page point that cites it for tracking food-service automation. The page may help a reader understand the association's scope, but it is not a source on AI adoption or automation in restaurants.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Hospitality

sections.body: This is a landing page with little substantive detail. It is promotional in tone and points to guides, programs, events, and news rather than presenting research findings. It does not cover AI, automation, robotics, predictive ordering, or drive-thru technology. It states no publication date and gives no data, methodology, or named author. The text is a partial snapshot of the association's homepage, so it may omit linked content. It does not substantiate the claim that the association tracks food-service automation.
